title: Updating an LRU stack
purpose: Show a referenced resident page being moved from middle to most-recent top, with other order preserved.
requiredChecks: Before-reference order from top to bottom is2,1,0,7,4.
Referencing7 produces after-order7,2,1,0,4; no duplicate7 is present.
Top is most recently used, bottom least recently used;4 remains bottom.
The requested page7 is identified, promotion arrow points toward the top of the after-stack, all text legible.
alt: LRU stack update on reference to page 7: move 7 from the middle to the most-recent position
prompt: Create a NEW original English technical educational diagram. White background, crisp large navy sans-serif text, flat blue/teal shapes, minimal clean connectors, generous margins, no logos or watermark, no decorative or traced textbook artwork. TITLE "Updating an LRU stack". Two separated vertical stacks with exactly five cells each. Left heading "Before reference to 7", TOP-TO-BOTTOM values2,1,0,7,4. Right heading "After reference to 7", TOP-TO-BOTTOM values7,2,1,0,4. Highlight the single7 cell in each stack teal. Above the right stack label "Most recently used"; below it label "Least recently used". One arrow in the clear gap between stacks goes from the left7 cell to the RIGHT TOP7 cell, with text "Move referenced page to the top". Keep the order of all other pages2,1,0,4 unchanged. Footer exactly "The bottom page is the LRU victim". Do not include ambiguous a/b time markers or the original reference-string artwork. No duplicated7, no removal of a different page.
sourceNote: Original a/b markers are ambiguous; use an explicit single reference-to-7 update, consistent with the original displayed stack orders.
